## Tests

- [ ] T1. Projection: every fixture envelope projects to an item whose MCTL payload is byte-identical to the envelope. An envelope with an extra field (for example `events/examples/invalid/body-field.json`) is rejected, audited and acked, never delivered.
- [ ] T2. Cross-tenant: a subscriber in tenant A with a matching `type` filter receives no event whose subject resolves to tenant B, and none whose subject resolves to no tenant.
- [ ] T3. Stale subscriber: an expired subscription, or one whose epoch was incremented after the event was claimed, is not delivered to. The drop is audited and not retried.
- [ ] T4. Spoofed event: the recipient rejects a delivery with a bad signature, a signature from a rotated-out secret after overlap ends, or a missing header. It accepts during the rotation overlap.
- [ ] T5. Replay: a timestamp outside tolerance is rejected. A re-sent `webhook-id` is rejected as a duplicate and causes no second side effect.
- [ ] T6. Duplicate redelivery: the same stream entry claimed twice (adapter restart before XACK) results in one accepted delivery at the recipient.
- [ ] T7. Cursor expiry: after trimming past MAXLEN, polling with an old cursor returns `cursor_expired`, never a silent skip. A fresh cursor resumes in order.
- [ ] T8. Recovery: a simulated adapter restart with pending entries resumes delivery via the XAUTOCLAIM-equivalent with `attempt > 1`.
- [ ] T9. Retry and dead-letter: 5xx responses and timeouts retry with backoff up to the budget, then dead-letter + ack + audit. 410 deactivates the subscription. 413 is not retried.
- [ ] T10. Backpressure: one stuck subscription exceeding its quota stops being claimed, while another subscription keeps receiving.
- [ ] T11. SSRF: rejected cases are http, userinfo, IP literal, 127.0.0.1, 10/8, 169.254.169.254, 100.64/10, ::1, fc00::/7, a port off the allowlist, and a redirect response. Also rejected is a resolver that answers public at registration and private at delivery (rebinding).
- [ ] T12. Challenge: activation fails on a wrong or echoed-twice challenge and succeeds only on a constant-time match. No delivery happens before activation.
- [ ] T13. Acks: host 2xx sets `delivered` only. `processed` is set only by an explicit processing ack call.
- [ ] T14. Audit: each stage writes one record containing the envelope `id`, `correlation_id` and subscription id, and no subject content beyond references.
- [ ] T15. Host fallback: with no `events` capability negotiated, the reference client falls back to polling with the same cursor semantics.
- [ ] T16. Manifest: `roadmap/scripts/validate.py` accepts the new SpikeDefinition, and the existing `events/tests/test_envelope_schema.py` still passes unchanged.

## Rollback

The spike changes only documentation, a roadmap manifest and offline model code
in `mctlhq/.github`. To roll back, revert the PR. No service, stream, ACL,
secret, host subscription or Claude Channel configuration is touched, so nothing
needs a runtime rollback. If the owner rejects the verdict, set the manifest
lifecycle to `parked` with an `activation.trigger` (for example "SEP-3415 reaches
Final and an SDK ships"), or `archived`, in a follow-up PR.
